content:
This is a discussion thread for the First Proof project -- a community experiment to test AI reasoning systems against novel (informal) math problems arising naturally in research.

Today, First Proof hosted a public webinar announcing that they have compiled their second batch of problems, and completed running multiple AI systems against those problems. They plan to announce the results next week after human experts have graded the solutions. More info about that event can be found here: #Event announcements > First Proof Second Batch

My impression from the webinar was that First Proof are well-aware of the methodological issues in the first batch, and the broader concerns about public "AI for Math" benchmarks (specifically, the fact that AI companies often fail to disclose their original prompts, compute cost, and level of human input).

I want to applaud the First Proof team for making the second batch a much more controlled experiment: teams submit their models ahead of time to be run on a dedicated server within a fixed 24-hour time window and without human input. They plan to collect data about the system architecture, prompts, and true token cost so that everything is transparent.
Interesting, curious which teams participated, e.g. did the big labs parttake directly. Can't find info yet, but we will know shortly.
@Michael R Douglas was this recorded, and will it be put on YouTube?
I'm very interested in the First Proof project, but does it have anything to do with Lean?
Probably nothing. But is this thread about Lean alone?
Please take a look at this thread's title.

Yes, I know that that's the thread's title, but since this Zulip is devoted to Lean, I thought that most people wanted to keep the discussion focused on Lean, rather than open it to arbitrary discussions about AI that are unrelated to Lean.

Why didn't you raise this issue from the start of this thread? Four other people have posted before me and none of the posts seems to have anything to do with Lean either. I was just following up by pointing out that the results of First Proof round 2 (which seems to be the topic of this thread) are out. (They were not out at the time of the last post before mine.) And who assigned you the role of policing the topical appropriateness anyway?

Ching-Tsun Chou said:

And who assigned you the role of policing the topical appropriateness anyway?

I'll leave another moderator to decide if this thread is inherently off-topic for this Zulip, but there is regardless no need to phrase this so aggressively. We all have a joint responsibility for keeping the Zulip on-topic, and I see nothing wrong with anyone politely pointing this out.
(if there is any work or discussion about formalizing any of the First Proof problems, that would certainly be relevant)

Note that my first reply was polite: "Please take a look at this thread's title." It seems to me that if a commenter considers my post to be off-topic, then he should consider all previous posts in this thread (and, for that matter, the thread of which this thread is a discussion thread) to be off-topic as well. After all, I was just providing an update to what was discussed before. So, why was my post singled out?

I don't see anyone singling out your post. Timothy's remark reads to me as a general comment about this thread. It makes sense that a low activity thread might not be noticed until such a follow up. It's a question of if this thread was on topic to begin with, not your specific messages.

Chris Henson is correct that I was not singling out anyone's post. I also didn't notice this thread until today. In fact, my first instinct was to make some observations about First Proof, but then I remembered that I have frequently seen longtime participants of this Zulip saying that discussions that have nothing to do with Lean are off-topic, so I thought I would ask before jumping in.

Let's for now consider this thread "closed". If there are people formalizing some of the proofs from the second batch, that's certainly on topic, and we can and should talk about that, but while the second batch remains formalization-free, let's just let this lie dormant.

(I think the difficulties upstream are mostly due to reasonable "it's hard to communicate on the internet", and everyone will forgive each other. Let's try to be considerate and assume good intent from each other. :-)
